title: Mess: how it works
summary: Mess complexes, cuisines including Jain mess, registration on iKollege, changing mess, rebates.

posts.md:
IIT Madras has **three major mess complexes**:

- Himalaya
- Vindhya
- Nilgiri

Together, they house **10–11 messes and food courts**, offering students a wide variety of meal options throughout the academic year.

The messes are designed to provide nutritious, hygienic, and diverse meals that cater to the needs of students from across the country.

## What Do the Messes Provide?

The messes are modern and student-friendly, featuring **face-scan biometric access** for seamless entry.

Across campus food courts, students can conveniently make payments using their **Institute ID cards**.

To cater to the diverse student community, IIT Madras has:

- North Indian Messes
- South Indian Messes
- Unified Messes serving both cuisines
- A Jain Mess for students who prefer Jain food

Students can choose familiar food from home or explore different cuisines.

The messes aim to meet the dietary requirements of all students without compromising on quality or nutrition.

## Mess Registration

Mess registration is managed through the **iKollege Portal**.

The system helps:

- Reduce food wastage by informing caterers about the expected number of diners.
- Ensure students do not pay for meals they do not consume.

## How to Register

Students can register for their preferred mess through the **iKollege Portal** during the dates announced by the **Office of Hostel Management**.

Students submit their mess preferences in order of choice.

Every effort is made to allot the **first preference**. However, if a mess reaches its capacity, students may be allotted another preference.

Mess allocation follows a **first-come, first-served** basis.

Students are also allowed to **change their mess** periodically (typically every one or two months).

Students staying on campus during vacations can also register for messes through the portal, provided they have the necessary accommodation and permission from the concerned authorities.

## What Makes IIT Madras' Mess System Unique?

Unlike many institutes where each hostel has its own mess, IIT Madras has **large common dining halls**, some with seating capacities of up to **1500 students**.

This allows students to interact with people from different hostels, departments, and academic years during meals.

The weekly menu offers sufficient variety to avoid monotony, and the food is also appreciated by many international students.

Students can also claim **mess rebates** for valid reasons such as:

- Ramadan fasting
- Health issues requiring recovery away from the Institute

The mess system is continuously improved in terms of food quality, management, and seating capacity to provide better services to students.
